claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing/full fiscal-year 2026 revenue for the first time.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion (up from $106 billion a year earlier).
AWS's AI business and its chips business (Trainium and Graviton) each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending will reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents.
Gartner predicts by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are standardizing on CNCF projects, and organizations are extending platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 82% agree AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal; Pulumi's report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence values the global Kubernetes market at USD 3.13 billion in 2026, projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, with 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
Inference workloads now require low-latency execution closer to the user, and Kubernetes is often the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration.
AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit (announced May 2026).
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
Pulumi Policies helps teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI.
Last year's edition of this piece predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade and the 2026 predictions held up.
